art.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge
art.holder: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
art.story: A summer storm breaks over the great bridge across the Sumida River in Edo, today's Tokyo. The downpour falls in fine dark lines, people hurry across under an umbrella and straw hats, and a lone raftsman poles his logs down the grey river. It is one of the One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, made the year before Hiroshige died. Van Gogh loved it so much that he copied it in oil paint, framed with Japanese characters.
